conviction_note: Balanced evidence: the robotaxi fleet stalled at >1,800 from 31 Jul to late Oct against a 2,600 year-end target, and the closest peer (Pony) beat revenue on 18 Nov and was sold 7.3%. Against that, WRD has already fallen about 21% in five sessions, mostly in sympathy with Pony's print and not on its own news, and GAC models with WRD 3.0 ADAS are selling well. abs_move 11 comes from the four confirmed prints (about +15, +9, -9 premarket, -9.7), with p_up 49, so expected = (2*0.49-1)*11 = -0.22. impact_sum is -0.6, the same sign and of similar size, so the two measurements do not conflict.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus is about RMB 270M, from two sources showing the same two-analyst pool: Yahoo (avg RMB 269.91M, range 234.7-305.1M, 2 analysts) https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/WRD/analysis and Chartmill (RMB 270.02M, revised sharply up over 3 months) https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/WRD/estimates (snippet only, 403 on fetch). That is +16.5% q/q on Q2's RMB 231.7M and +58% y/y on Q3 2025's RMB 171.0M. The EPS bar is a single analyst at -0.99 (currency unclear), so it is not usable. The company gives no revenue guidance. Its standing operating targets are 2,600 robotaxis by end-2026 (stated 23 Mar 2026, 'subject to market and regulatory conditions') and 100,000 L2++/L3 units by year-end. The bar rests on only two analysts, so every finding is capped small.

expectations.real_bar: After a beat was sold in August and Pony's beat-and-reaffirm was sold on 18 Nov, revenue above RMB 270M will not lift the stock alone. It needs a credible robotaxi fleet path to the 2,600 year-end target (or a clear explanation of the Q3 stall), ADAS volume tracking toward 100k, and a narrower loss or a fresh buyback.

next_guide.company_current_guide: No revenue guide. Operating targets: 2,600 robotaxis by end-2026 (23 Mar 2026 release https://ir.weride.ai/news-releases/news-release-details/weride-reports-record-full-year-2025-revenue-rmb6846-million-90), more than 100,000 L2++/L3 units by end-2026 and 500,000 in 2027 (Q2 call, https://quartr.com/events/weride-inc-wrd-q2-2026_FYc1ExDA), operating cash flow positive in a single quarter by 2028, break-even in 2029.
next_guide.basis: The robotaxi count was 'more than 1,800' on both 31 Jul and the 27 Oct release, so +800 in about two months depends on the Geely Farizon GXR ramp that starts in Q3. That points to cut or maintain-with-caveat on the fleet target. Pony maintained its 3,500 target on 18 Nov, and the GAC ADAS model sales support the 100k target. Net direction is unknown.

findings.finding: The robotaxi fleet did not grow during Q3. The Q2 release counted 'more than 1,800 robotaxis' (about 3,400 AVs) as of 31 Jul 2026, and the 27 Oct 2026 insurance-program release still says 'more than 1,800 Robotaxis' (about 3,600 AVs). Reaching the 2,600 end-2026 target therefore needs about +800 robotaxis in roughly two months. Pony, by contrast, had 2,768 at 30 Sep and kept its 3,500 target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Fleet targets are the stock's narrative anchor. The Q2 print (fleet +500 q/q, overseas fleet doubled) still fell 9.7%, so fleet growth alone has not lifted the stock, but a stall or a cut has not yet been tested.
findings.why_not_priced: The fleet figure sat in an insurance-program press release, not a results release, and no preview found compares it with the 31 Jul count. Earnings Whispers on 15 Nov still describes the 2,600 target as 'unchanged'. If the market had priced the stall, previews would be asking whether the target holds. Part of the 25% week may be this, but the drawdown tracked Pony's day by day, which points to a sector move rather than a company one.
findings.independence: The Q2 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001867729/000110465926094571/tm2622690d2_ex99-1.htm, 12 Aug 2026) gives the 31 Jul baseline of more than 1,800 robotaxis. The target and its 'subject to conditions' caveat are in the 23 Mar 2026 release. The Geely Farizon GXR upgrade rolling off production in Q3 2026 (https://finviz.com/news/333226/weride-and-geely-farizon-to-deliver-2000-purpose-built-robotaxi-gxrs-by-2026-advancing-large-scale-global-commercialization) is the path by which the stall could reverse in Q4. 'More than 1,800' is a floor, so the true October count could be somewhat higher.

findings.finding: Peer read-through. Pony AI reported Q3 2026 on 18 Nov before the open: revenue of US$44.6M (+75% y/y) against Benzinga's pre-report estimate of $39.1M, robotaxi revenue +165%, gross margin down to 17.8%, and the 3,500-vehicle and 3.5x robotaxi revenue targets reaffirmed. PONY fell 7.3% that day (3.99 to 3.70 on 11.9M shares, about 4x average) and about 4.7% more on 19 Nov. The market sold a beat-and-reaffirm in the same business, the same quarter, two days before WRD reports.
findings.link: Same product and markets: Chinese L4 robotaxi operators, both on Uber's platform in the Middle East and Europe, both dual-listed in New York and Hong Kong (both listed in HK on 6 Nov 2025), both reporting the September quarter. Robotaxi is about 40% of Pony's revenue; WRD's L4 line was 54% of revenue in Q2 2026.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: WRD moved -7.1% on Pony's results day, on 2.4x its normal volume, so this peer's prints transmit directly. In April 2025 the two moved in opposite directions on a Pony product event.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: WRD has already fallen about 17% since Pony reported. What is not settled is the reaction function, that a sector beat with reaffirmed targets was sold, which applies to WRD's own release tomorrow. Had WRD fully discounted it, there would be no further drift into the print, yet it was still falling about 10% intraday on 19 Nov.
findings.independence: Prices are from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/PONY?range=1mo&interval=1d. The Pony estimate is from Benzinga (https://benzinga.com/z/49055208, snippet only). This shares the Yahoo tape with the expectations finding below, but reads a different object (the peer's reaction to a beat versus WRD's own drawdown).

findings.finding: Expectations are already compressed into the print. WRD is -21.3% over 5 sessions and -22.6% over about 20, against KWEB's -5.8% and -9.1%, at a fresh 52-week low ($3.305 intraday on 19 Nov) and about 75% below the stale average target of about $14. The fall coincides with Pony's print and peer selling, not with any WRD filing (the last WRD 6-K was the 6 Nov board-meeting notice).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 2025 came after a roughly -20% run-in around the HK listing and rose about 15% on the print. Q2 2026 came after a less depressed setup and fell 9.7% on a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: This is the price itself. The claim is that the bar is lowered: a sector-driven 21% fall with no company news means a merely adequate release (fleet target held, ADAS on track) can rebound. If the market had separated WRD from Pony's own issues (Pony's margin fell, WRD's was a record 37.5% in Q2), WRD would not have tracked Pony day for day.
findings.independence: EDGAR filing list (https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK0001867729.json): no WRD 6-K after 6 Nov 2026. The Earnings Whispers preview of 15 Nov reports bearish sentiment up to about 59%. Lesson 5 warns that an unexplained drawdown is worth 0, but here the cause is identifiable (the peer print), which is why this is sized and not zero.

findings.finding: Customer volume supports the ADAS line. GAC Aion N60, the first mass-production car with WeRide's WRD 3.0 one-stage ADAS, passed 20,000 users in under five months, and Aion i60 orders passed 20,000 by end-September (the i60 runs on WRD 3.0 per WeRide's 15 Sep 2026 release). GAC Hyper/Aion BU sold 35,494 units in September, +21.9% y/y. Q2 L2++/L3 deliveries were about 30,000 units, worth roughly RMB 106M (total revenue less L4).
findings.link: GAC Aion is a WRD 3.0 customer. The N60 and i60 are named WRD 3.0 programs. Per-unit ADAS revenue is roughly RMB 3,500 (Q2 non-L4 revenue of about RMB 106M over about 30k units), and ADAS was about 46% of Q2 revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The ADAS ramp drove Q2's +103% q/q revenue jump. That beat was sold (-9.7%) because the loss did not narrow, so the line has paid on the number but not on the stock.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus of RMB 270M implies only +16.5% q/q after a +103% quarter. If the ADAS run-rate held at or above 30k units with N60/i60 volumes, the street would be nearer the top of its range (RMB 305M) than the middle. The September sales data comes from Chinese auto press that ADR previews do not cite.
findings.independence: GAC September sales: https://auto.sina.cn/newcar/2026-10-01/detail-inittqyc6523039.d.html. WRD 3.0 on the i60: WeRide release of 15 Sep 2026 (stocktitan news list https://www.stocktitan.net/news/WRD/). This is a proxy, not a WeRide unit count. Customer user counts are cumulative marketing figures, not monthly deliveries.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is likely to clear the RMB 270M bar. It needs only +16.5% q/q on Q2's RMB 231.7M, which itself followed Q1's 114.1M. Q4 seasonality (Q4 2025 was 314M, with heavy product sales) means the street has back-loaded the year (Q4 consensus 514M). But this name sold its last beat (Q2 revenue beat, -9.7%).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue line: Q1 2026 miss, about -9% pre-market. Q2 2026 beat, -9.7% close. Q4 2025 beat plus buyback, +9%. Q3 2025 +144%, about +15%. A beat alone has paid one time in two.
findings.why_not_priced: A consensus beat is the base case and is mostly priced. It is filed small because the bar is two analysts wide (RMB 234.7-305.1M).
findings.independence: Chartmill RMB 270.02M (snippet only, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/WRD/estimates) draws on the same small pool. This shares its basis with the ADAS counterparty finding (which is why the latter is the larger of the two).

findings.finding: The buyback is largely spent and paused. The HKEX monthly return for October 2026 shows 40,454,099 Class A shares in treasury and issued shares unchanged in the month, against 25.16M treasury shares on 13 May 2026. At the roughly $2.2-2.5 per-share prices of the May-June buying, 40.45M shares is about $90-100M, close to the $100M program approved in March 2026, which runs until March 2027. A re-authorisation at the print is possible. The last buyback announcement (with Q4 2025) coincided with +9%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 23 Mar 2026: Q4 results plus a $100M buyback, +9% (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/WRD/we-ride-reports-record-full-year-2025-revenue-of-rmb684-6-million-up-jk4jsjcttsk5.html).
findings.why_not_priced: Treasury accounting is in an HKEX form, not a wire story, and no preview mentions that the program is near exhaustion. Sign is ambiguous: losing the support bid is negative, while a re-up at a 52-week low with about $790M of cash would be positive. Net sized small and positive with a wide band.
findings.independence: May treasury count and buy prices: https://www.itiger.com/news/1102482285 (14 May 2026). Treasury shares may not all come from this program, so the dollar estimate is an inference.

findings.finding: Reaction function: across the four confirmed prints the stock moved about +15%, +9%, about -9% (pre-market) and -9.7%. The last two prints were both sold, including a revenue beat with a record gross margin in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: As stated: two up, then two down, the most recent being down on a beat.
findings.why_not_priced: History, not new information. Filed because the baseline's 6-K-matched history is not usable (it counts operational 6-Ks as prints), so this is the rebuilt base rate.

findings.finding: Working-capital quality: a Sina Finance analysis (11 Sep 2026) reports WeRide's receivable turnover days rising to 239 in H1 2026, against 86 at Pony, and inventory up 36.8% in H1. Product revenue is being booked ahead of cash collection.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Not tested on a print. Q2's beat was sold on loss and profitability concerns.
findings.why_not_priced: Chinese-language balance-sheet analysis that the ADR coverage does not cite. It would matter if Q3 shows receivables still rising alongside product revenue.

findings.finding: Middle East macro (counterparty commentary): on its 4 Nov 2026 call, Uber's CFO cited 'escalation in the war in the Middle East' and fuel-cost impacts, and expects about 700 fully driverless vehicles on Uber by year-end and more than 2,000 by end-2027. About 400 of WeRide's robotaxis are in the Middle East (31 Jul), mostly on Uber. In March 2026 the Iran conflict made WeRide suspend Dubai (Abu Dhabi and Riyadh kept running), and Dubai driverless fare-charging resumed in April.
findings.link: Uber is WeRide's platform partner in Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Riyadh (commitment of at least 1,200 robotaxis across the three cities). Uber did not name WeRide on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The March 2026 Dubai suspension came before Q4 2025 results, which still rose 9%.
findings.why_not_priced: A transmission from macro to the company that neither WeRide nor Uber has confirmed. It is a proxy, filed small.
findings.independence: March suspension: https://www.timeslive.co.za/motoring/2026-03-03-weride-suspends-robotaxi-fleet-in-dubai-as-iran-conflict-widens/. April Dubai driverless launch: https://www.intelligentcio.com/me/2026/04/13/weride-and-uber-launch-fully-driverless-robotaxi-fare-charging-operations-in-dubai-accelerating-autonomous-mobility-in-the-middle-east/

findings.finding: Governance item: on 28-29 Oct 2026 WeRide agreed to let its PRC data subsidiary Jingshuo take RMB 70M from outside investors and adopt an equity scheme that gives each co-founder (Han, Huo) RMB 8M of registered capital. WeRide's stake falls from 100% to about 67.6%. Jingshuo had 2025 revenue of RMB 187.1M and a loss of RMB 31.2M. The company says there is no material P&L effect.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced on the day. It could resurface on the call if analysts ask about co-founders holding equity in a carve-out. It is below operating income with no path to the guide, so it is sized as a fraction.

findings.finding: The CTO and director Li Yan received an RSU award of 493,434 Class A shares on 23 Sep 2026 that vests only on reaching unspecified revenue targets. It is a grant, not a purchase or sale. No open-market insider trades were found.
findings.independence: Three other Form 4s were filed the same day (not opened).

outside_window.finding: Madrid robotaxi commercial operations with Uber and AVOMO are expected by end-2026 (national L4 permit 10 Sep 2026, initial fleet of 20). A European revenue start is a Q4 or 2027 item.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The evidence is split around the run-in: the fleet stall and the peer's sold beat point down, while the 21% sector-driven fall into the print and the ADAS customer volumes point to a lowered bar. The net is a near-zero lean, not a call against the run-up.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the consensus-beat finding was cut from +0.5 to +0.2 because the Q2 beat was sold (-9.7%).
Lesson 1 and the core table: the reaction-history finding was cut from -0.5 to -0.3, so the same 'this name sells beats' concern is not counted twice. p_up moved from 48 to 49.
Lesson 5 (proxy): the Middle East macro finding was cut from -0.3 to -0.2 because no company or counterparty confirmed it.
Lesson 6 (thin bar): the bar is two estimate sources drawing on one two-analyst pool, so every finding stays capped small. Left as drafted.
Lesson 7 (positioning): short interest was checked before filing negatives. At 7.4% of free float it is not crowded, so the negatives are not shrunk.
Lesson 9 (segment): the fleet stall is an L4 finding, netted against the ADAS counterparty finding. Left at -1.5 because it lands on the guide, not the quarter.
Base rate rebuilt from the four confirmed prints, as the lesson on untrustworthy histories requires: abs_move stays at 11.
A CTO RSU grant was added at 0.0 for breadth (not in the draft sum).
